question.:question/problem:
Consider the augmented matrix $M$ given by

$$
M=\left[\begin{array}{cc|c}2 & -8 & 18 \\ 3 & -7 & -18\end{array}\right].
$$

Use the standard method of Gaussian elimination to reduce $M$ to row echelon form.
question.:question/worked-solution:
Reducing $M$ to row echelon form using the standard algorithm for Gaussian elimination, we have

$$
\begin{aligned}M & ∼\left[\begin{array}{cc|c}2 & -8 & 18 \\ 3 & -7 & -18\end{array}\right] & {R}_{1} & :=\frac{1}{2}{R}_{1} \\  & ∼\left[\begin{array}{cc|c}1 & -4 & 9 \\ 3 & -7 & -18\end{array}\right] & {R}_{2} & :={R}_{2}+(-3){R}_{1} \\  & ∼\left[\begin{array}{cc|c}1 & -4 & 9 \\ 0 & 5 & -45\end{array}\right] & {R}_{2} & :=\frac{1}{5}{R}_{2} \\  & ∼\left[\begin{array}{cc|c}1 & -4 & 9 \\ 0 & 1 & -9\end{array}\right].\end{aligned}
$$

question.:question/problem:
Consider the augmented matrix $M$ given by

$$
M=\left[\begin{array}{cc|c}3 & 9 & 24 \\ 2 & 7 & 12\end{array}\right].
$$

Use the standard method of Gaussian elimination to reduce $M$ to row echelon form, and then solve the linear system represented by the matrix.
question.:question/worked-solution:
Reducing $M$ to row echelon form, we have

$$
\begin{aligned}M & ∼\left[\begin{array}{cc|c}3 & 9 & 24 \\ 2 & 7 & 12\end{array}\right] & {R}_{1} & :=\frac{1}{3}{R}_{1} \\  & ∼\left[\begin{array}{cc|c}1 & 3 & 8 \\ 2 & 7 & 12\end{array}\right] & {R}_{2} & :={R}_{2}-2\cdot {R}_{1} \\  & ∼\left[\begin{array}{cc|c}1 & 3 & 8 \\ 0 & 1 & -4\end{array}\right].\end{aligned}
$$

The system is now

$$
\left\{\begin{aligned}x+3y &=8 \\ y &=-4\end{aligned}\right.
$$

and we can apply back substitution. The final equation $y=-4$ tells us the value of $y.$ Substituting this value into the first equation, we get

$$
x+3\left(-4\right)=8\,\Rightarrow\,x=8+12=20.
$$

Therefore, the solution is $x=20$ and $y=-4.$
